key_insight: Supersonic turbulent shear layers become self-similar downstream across Mach number and velocity-parameter variations, but compressibility and advection strongly reshape growth, asymmetry, and entrainment.
engineering_relevance: These results provide scaling laws and closed-form approximations useful for predicting mixing and entrainment in high-speed propulsion, jets, and other compressible shear-flow systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of spatially developing supersonic turbulent shear layers.
Parameter sweep over convective Mach number (Mc) and velocity parameter (λ).
Derivation of self-similar forms for continuity, momentum, and energy, plus an approximate cross-stream velocity and entrainment ratio equation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports collapse of normalized velocity and turbulence profiles in the self-similar region, linear thickness growth, and good agreement between the approximate cross-stream velocity equation and DNS results.
watch_item: The proposed scalings and closed-form relations are validated in DNS cases for the studied parameter range, so extrapolation to other geometries, Reynolds numbers, or stronger nonequilibrium regimes should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Compressibility and Velocity Parameter Effects on Spatially Evolving Supersonic Turbulent Shear Layers
